# API Reference

Production-grade integration reference for the Synora Face ID backend.

**Base URL** (default): `http://<host>:8000`
**API prefix**: all REST endpoints are mounted under `/api/v1/…`
**Interactive docs** (auto-generated by FastAPI):
  * Swagger UI — `GET /docs`
  * ReDoc — `GET /redoc`
  * OpenAPI JSON — `GET /openapi.json`

Verified against codebase as of `2026-05-24`.

## 1. Conventions

* **Transport**: HTTP/1.1, JSON request and response bodies unless noted (multipart for uploads, MJPEG/WS for streaming).
* **Encoding**: UTF-8.
* **Time**: server returns ISO-8601 with timezone (or naive when the DB column has no tz). Clients should parse defensively.
* **Identifiers**:
  * `user_id` / `patient_id` — auto-increment integer.
  * `camera_id` — slug of shape `cam_[a-z0-9_]+`, assigned server-side, **stable for the lifetime of any session that references it**.
  * `mrn` — caller-provided string, unique across `user_type=PATIENT`.
* **Pagination**: not implemented. Where a list endpoint exposes a `limit` query, it is documented inline; defaults differ per endpoint (`/users` → 200, `/frontdesk/search` → 10, `/frontdesk/patients/{id}/visits` → 50). For larger result sets, filter first (`?type=…`, `?q=…`).
* **Idempotency**: POST endpoints are not idempotent unless explicitly stated. PATCH is partial-merge; PUT on `/users/{id}` is a legacy alias that mostly mirrors PATCH but routes pure-demographic updates through a path that also propagates `name` changes to FAISS labels — see §8 for the distinction.

### File uploads

Multipart uploads (`POST /register/multi`, `POST /recognize`, `POST /frontdesk/scan`, `POST /users/{id}/update-face/multi`):

* Field name carrying the image is documented per endpoint.
* JPEG (`\xff\xd8\xff`) and PNG (`\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n`) only — content is sniffed by magic bytes, not by extension.
* Hard cap **5 MiB per image**. Larger files are rejected before they reach OpenCV.

## 2. Authentication & CORS

Authentication uses the canonical `users` identity. Employees and doctors may
receive an optional credential, role, and permission overrides. Non-human
service accounts are reserved for external integrations.

### Session model

* **Cookie sessions, not header tokens.** `POST /auth/login` sets an HttpOnly, signed session cookie carrying the principal kind and canonical user/service ID, plus a readable CSRF cookie (`iris_csrf`).
* Send `credentials: 'include'` on fetches. On mutating requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), echo the `iris_csrf` cookie value in an `X-CSRF-Token` header (double-submit CSRF; enforced only when `AUTH_ENABLED=true`).
* Sessions expire after `SESSION_TTL_HOURS` (default 12h). Login is rate-limited: after `LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` failures per (username, IP), further attempts return `429` for `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES`.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Body / Notes | Success |
| ------ | ---- | ------------ | ------- |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/auth/login` | `{ "username", "password" }` | `200` → `{ id, username, role, permissions[] }`, sets cookies |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/auth/logout` | — | `200`, clears cookies (idempotent) |
| `GET`  | `/api/v1/auth/me` | requires session cookie | `200` → same shape as login; `401` if unauthenticated |

`permissions[]` is the principal's effective permission set. Bootstrap the
facility and first superadmin with `python -m backend.scripts.seed_initial`.

### Account management (`/api/v1/auth/accounts`)

Guarded by `accounts.manage_staff` (which `super_admin` also holds). Mutating calls require the `X-CSRF-Token` header.

| Method | Path | Notes |
| ------ | ---- | ----- |
| `GET`  | `/auth/accounts` | Users that currently have login access. |
| `GET`  | `/auth/accounts/candidates` | Active employees/doctors eligible for access. |
| `POST` | `/auth/accounts` | `{ user_id, username, password, role }`; grants access to an existing user. |
| `PATCH`| `/auth/accounts/{user_id}` | Change role or enable/disable login. |
| `PATCH`| `/auth/accounts/{user_id}/permissions` | Apply per-user grants/revocations. |

### Audit log (`/api/v1/audit`)

Guarded by `audit.read`. Append-only trail of security-relevant actions (logins + failures, account create/update/permission changes, camera create/update/delete). Read-only — there is no delete/edit surface.

| Method | Path | Notes |
| ------ | ---- | ----- |
| `GET`  | `/audit?limit=&offset=&action=` | Newest first. `limit` 1–500 (default 100); `action` filters to an exact action string (e.g. `auth.login`). |

### Enforcement map

Every router carries a permission guard (`backend/app/api/router.py` is the single map). `facility`/`locations` use `locations.manage`; all guards are inert until `AUTH_ENABLED=true`.

`locations.manage` and `integrations.manage` are admin-tier defaults.

### Roles & permissions

Three roles — `staff`, `admin`, `super_admin` — are bundles of named permissions (`frontdesk.operate`, `users.read`, `streams.view`, `cameras.manage`, …). Individual accounts can be granted extra permissions or have some revoked, so, e.g., a specific front-desk `staff` account can be given `streams.view` without a role change. See the `auth-rbac` plan for the full matrix and grant hierarchy.

### CORS

CORS is wired via the standard `CORSMiddleware`:

* Allowed origins: `settings.ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (env `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, comma-separated or JSON array). Defaults to `*` in development — **must be an explicit origin list in production** because credentialed (cookie) requests are incompatible with a `*` origin.
* Credentials enabled; methods and headers permissive.

## 3. Errors

Errors follow the FastAPI default shape:

```json
{ "detail": "human-readable message" }
```

For Pydantic validation failures (status `422`), `detail` is an array describing each field that failed validation.

| Status | Meaning in this service |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| `200`  | Success. |
| `201`  | Resource created. Returned by `POST /users`, `POST /cameras`, `POST /users/{id}/relations`. |
| `204`  | Success with no body. Returned by DELETE endpoints. |
| `400`  | Bad request — malformed image, unknown `user_type`, missing required field per type, invalid DOB format, etc. |
| `404`  | Resource not found. |
| `409`  | Conflict — duplicate MRN, duplicate camera name, duplicate department code/token_prefix, etc. |
| `422`  | Pydantic validation error. |
| `500`  | Internal error. Indicates a bug; should be reported with the request body. |
| `503`  | Service not ready — typically the camera system has not booted (`START_CAMERA_SYSTEM` env var unset) and the caller hit a camera-admin route. |

`NoFaceDetectedError` from the face service surfaces as `400` with `detail` describing which image had no detectable face.

---

## 4. Data model summary

A single `users` table holds every identity. The discriminator is `user_type`:

* `PATIENT` — clinical patient. Requires `mrn`.
* `DOCTOR` — clinician. Requires `opd_department_id`.
* `EMPLOYEE` — staff. Requires `role`.
* `VISITOR` — short-stay guest. `purpose` recommended.
* `RELATIVE` — accompanies a patient. Linked to one or more patients via `/users/{id}/relations`.

A second table `user_relations` carries (`user_id`, `related_user_id`, `relation_type`, `note`). `relation_type` is one of `SPOUSE | PARENT | CHILD | SIBLING | GUARDIAN | OTHER`.

`patients`, `doctors`, and the old per-type tables have been folded into `users` (see `docs/CHANGELOG.md` Phases 1–8). The `/patients/*` routes documented in §10 are alias shims, retained for legacy integrators only.

Face embeddings live in a separate FAISS index keyed by `user_id`. Face operations do **not** go through `/users` PATCH — they have a dedicated multipart endpoint at `POST /users/{id}/update-face/multi`.

### Common user fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
| ----- | ---- | ----- |
| `id` | int | Auto-increment. |
| `user_type` | enum | One of `PATIENT \| DOCTOR \| EMPLOYEE \| VISITOR \| RELATIVE`. |
| `name` | string | Required. 1–255 chars. |
| `mrn` | string \| null | Unique when present; required for `PATIENT`. |
| `age` | int \| null | |
| `gender` | string \| null | Free-form (UI convention: `M`, `F`, `Other`). |
| `dob` | date \| null | `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `contact_number` | string \| null | |
| `address` | string \| null | |
| `department` | string \| null | Patient legacy free-text department label. |
| `doctor` | string \| null | Patient legacy free-text assigned doctor. |
| `category` | string \| null | Patient legacy category tag. |
| `role` | string \| null | Required for `EMPLOYEE`. |
| `specialty` | string \| null | Doctor speciality. |
| `staff_department` | string \| null | Structured department name for staff. |
| `opd_department_id` | int \| null | FK → frontdesk department. Required for `DOCTOR`. |
| `opd_room_id` | int \| null | FK → frontdesk room. |
| `purpose` | string \| null | Visitor purpose. |
| `note` | string \| null | Free-form. |
| `is_active` | bool | Soft-delete flag. |
| `current_status` | `"IN" \| "OUT"` | Set by the tracking pipeline; **read-only over the API**. |
| `current_floor` | string \| null | Read-only. |
| `current_camera_id` | string \| null | Read-only. |
| `last_seen_at` | datetime \| null | Read-only. |
| `created_at` | datetime | Read-only. |

## 5. Health

### `GET /api/v1/health`

Liveness probe. Returns immediately without touching the DB or FAISS.

**Response 200**

```json
{ "status": "ok" }
```

Use for `livenessProbe`. For `readinessProbe`, prefer a lightweight read like `GET /api/v1/users?limit=1` so you also catch a dead Postgres. `GET /` (without the API prefix) is also routed and returns `{"app", "version", "docs"}` — useful as a non-DB-touching readiness signal.

---

## 6. Registration (enrol a face)

### `POST /api/v1/register/multi`

Enrol a new identity with one or more aligned face images. Each image is detected, aligned, embedded independently (ArcFace 512-d), and stored as a separate embedding under the same `user_id`. The endpoint is type-agnostic — supply `user_type` to skip the legacy patient flow and create a doctor / employee / visitor / relative row directly.

Recommended capture: **5–10 images** covering frontal, slight left, slight right, looking up, looking down. Images with no detectable face are silently skipped and reported under `skipped[]`.

**Content-Type**: `multipart/form-data`

| Form field | Type | Required | Notes |
| ---------- | ---- | -------- | ----- |
| `name` | string | yes | Display label. Bound to the FAISS row. |
| `images` | file (repeat) | yes | 1..N JPEG/PNG images. Capped server-side at `MAX_EMBEDDINGS_PER_IDENTITY` (10 by default). |
| `user_type` | string | no | `PATIENT \| DOCTOR \| EMPLOYEE \| VISITOR \| RELATIVE`. Defaults to `PATIENT`. |
| `age`, `gender`, `dob` | mixed | no | Demographics. `dob` is `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `contact_number`, `address` | string | no | |
| `department`, `doctor`, `category` | string | no | Patient legacy fields. |
| `role`, `specialty`, `staff_department` | string | no | Doctor / employee. |
| `opd_department_id`, `opd_room_id` | int | no | Doctor placement. |
| `purpose` | string | no | Visitor. |
| `note` | string | no | Free-form. |

> `mrn` is **not** a form field — for `user_type=PATIENT`, a unique MRN is auto-generated server-side (with retry on collision). For non-patient types, no MRN is issued. Use `POST /users` (§8) if you need to supply a specific MRN at create time.

**Response 200**

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "user_id": 42,
  "name": "Asha Devi",
  "mrn": "MRN-00042",
  "embeddings_stored": 7,
  "photo_url": "/media/profile_photos/9f1c2e64-….jpg",
  "skipped": [
    { "filename": "img3.jpg", "reason": "no face detected" }
  ]
}
```

`mrn` is auto-issued and returned for `user_type=PATIENT` only; absent / `null` for other types.

`photo_url` — the first uploaded image with a usable face is saved as the profile photo (re-encoded to a clean JPEG — original bytes/EXIF are discarded; filename is the random `person_guid`, so URLs are not enumerable). Served from the API's `/media/*` mount, or from `MEDIA_BASE_URL` once a dedicated media server is configured (see CONFIGURATION.md §2). `null` if photo storage failed (best-effort — never fails the registration). The same field also appears on user objects (§8) and is refreshed by `update-face/multi`. `skipped` is omitted entirely when every uploaded image passed validation; `reason` strings come from the upload-validator (`"empty file"`, `"too large (… bytes …)"`, `"unsupported format (only JPEG/PNG allowed)"`, `"could not decode image"`). A separate `NoFaceDetectedError` (`400`) fires only when **no** image yielded a detectable face.

**Errors**

* `400` — empty `name`, no images, all images rejected (with first reason in `detail`), invalid DOB.
* `400` — `NoFaceDetectedError`: none of the supplied images had a detectable face.
* `500` — unexpected pipeline error.

**curl example**

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/register/multi \
  -F "name=Asha Devi" \
  -F "user_type=PATIENT" \
  -F "age=34" \
  -F "gender=F" \
  -F "images=@front.jpg" \
  -F "images=@left.jpg" \
  -F "images=@right.jpg"
```

**Python example**

```python
import requests

files = [("images", open(p, "rb")) for p in ("front.jpg", "left.jpg", "right.jpg")]
data = {"name": "Asha Devi", "user_type": "PATIENT", "age": 34, "gender": "F"}
r = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/api/v1/register/multi", data=data, files=files)
r.raise_for_status()
print(r.json())  # {"success": True, "user_id": 42, "name": "Asha Devi", "mrn": "MRN-…", "embeddings_stored": 3}
```

## 7. Recognition (one-shot)

### `POST /api/v1/recognize`

Run detection + recognition on a single uploaded frame. Returns every detected face with its best FAISS match (or `"Unknown"` when no match passes `SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD`, default `0.60` — the value in [`backend/config.py`](../backend/config.py), which the FAISS path reads at module load).

**Content-Type**: `multipart/form-data`

| Form field | Type | Required |
| ---------- | ---- | -------- |
| `image` | file | yes |

**Response 200**

```json
{
  "faces": [
    {
      "identity": "Asha Devi",
      "user_id": 42,
      "confidence": 0.87,
      "bbox": [310, 142, 524, 392]
    },
    {
      "identity": "Unknown",
      "confidence": 0.31,
      "bbox": [88, 160, 234, 348]
    }
  ]
}
```

An empty `faces` array is **not** an error — it just means the detector saw nothing. The `user_id` key is **absent** (not `null`) on `Unknown` results.

**Errors**

* `400` — image could not be decoded.

For multi-face workflows where you also need to surface "who else is in the frame" for one-click queue swap, use `POST /frontdesk/scan` (§14) instead — it adds bbox-area ranking and embeds the full user record per candidate.

---

## 8. Users (unified user model)

### `GET /api/v1/users`

List users.

| Query | Type | Default | Notes |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----- |
| `type` | string | — | Filter by `user_type`. |
| `q` | string | — | Free-text ILIKE against `name`, `mrn`, `contact_number`. |
| `is_active` | bool | `true` | Pass `false` to return only soft-deleted rows. There is no way to fetch both in one call — query twice and merge if you need everything. |
| `limit` | int | `200` | Hard cap server-side. |

**Response 200** — array of [user objects](#common-user-fields), ordered by `name` ascending.

### `POST /api/v1/users`

Create a user **without** face data. Use `POST /users/{id}/update-face/multi` afterwards to enrol face samples, or `POST /register/multi` to do both at once.

**Body**

```json
{
  "user_type": "PATIENT",
  "name": "Asha Devi",
  "mrn": "MRN-00042",
  "age": 34,
  "gender": "F",
  "contact_number": "+91-9000000000"
}
```

Required-by-type fields are enforced server-side (see §4). Unknown keys are silently dropped.

**Response 201** — full user object.

**Errors**

* `400` — invalid `user_type`, missing per-type required field, duplicate MRN.

### `GET /api/v1/users/{user_id}`

User detail **plus** every relation the user participates in (either direction).

**Response 200**

```json
{
  "id": 42,
  "user_type": "PATIENT",
  "name": "Asha Devi",
  "mrn": "MRN-00042",
  "is_active": true,
  "current_status": "IN",
  "current_floor": "floor_2",
  "current_camera_id": "cam_lobby_2f",
  "last_seen_at": "2026-05-24T09:12:44+00:00",
  "relations": [
    {
      "id": 7,
      "user_id": 42,
      "related_user_id": 51,
      "relation_type": "GUARDIAN",
      "related_user_name": "Ravi Devi",
      "related_user_type": "RELATIVE",
      "note": null,
      "created_at": "2026-05-20T11:02:11+00:00"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Errors**: `404` — unknown user.

### `PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}`

Partial update. Only keys present in the body are written; everything else is left as-is. The `current_*`, `last_seen_at`, and FAISS-owned fields are **not writable**.

**Response 200** — updated user.

**Errors**

* `400` — invalid `user_type`.
* `404` — unknown user.

### `PUT /api/v1/users/{user_id}`

Legacy alias of `PATCH`. Kept so older clients continue to work. **Subtle difference**: a PUT containing only legacy patient demographics (`name`, `age`, `gender`, `dob`, `contact_number`, `address`, `department`, `doctor`, `category`, `mrn`) routes through `face_service.update_user_full`, which also propagates a `name` change to FAISS labels. A PATCH always uses `user_service.update_user`. If you change `name`, prefer PUT so the on-screen MJPEG overlay updates immediately.

### `DELETE /api/v1/users/{user_id}`

Delete a user.

| Query | Type | Default | Notes |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----- |
| `soft` | bool | `false` | When true, flips `is_active=false` and keeps the FAISS embedding + history. |

A hard delete (`soft=false`) purges the FAISS row and any face thumbnails on disk but **preserves** session history (the `patient_sessions` rows remain, but join to the (now absent) user row will return `null`).

**Response 204** — no body.

### `POST /api/v1/users/{user_id}/update-face/multi`

Replace the user's face embeddings with a new multi-angle batch. Same upload shape as `POST /register/multi` but only the `images` field is read.

**Content-Type**: `multipart/form-data`

| Form field | Type | Required |
| ---------- | ---- | -------- |
| `images` | file (repeat) | yes |

**Response 200**

```json
{ "success": true, "user_id": 42, "name": "Asha Devi", "embeddings_stored": 7 }
```

The endpoint **replaces** the user's embeddings — every prior FAISS entry under this `user_id` is purged before the new batch is written.

**Errors**

* `400` — no valid images, `NoFaceDetectedError`.
* `404` — unknown user.

---

## 9. User relations

### `GET /api/v1/users/{user_id}/relations`

Every relation involving the user, in either direction. Each row carries `related_user_name` and `related_user_type` so the client does not need a second round-trip.

### `POST /api/v1/users/{user_id}/relations`

Link `related_user_id` to `{user_id}` with the given `relation_type`. Both directions are surfaced by the GET above — do **not** call this twice for the same pair.

**Body**

```json
{
  "related_user_id": 51,
  "relation_type": "GUARDIAN",
  "note": "primary contact"
}
```

`relation_type`: one of `SPOUSE | PARENT | CHILD | SIBLING | GUARDIAN | OTHER` (free string accepted at API level; service layer validates).

**Response 201** — the relation row.

**Errors**

* `400` — invalid `relation_type`, self-link, or `related_user_id` doesn't exist.
* `404` — `{user_id}` doesn't exist.

### `DELETE /api/v1/users/{user_id}/relations/{relation_id}`

Unlink. The path `user_id` is preserved for URL symmetry; only `relation_id` identifies the row.

**Response 204**. `404` if the relation is gone.

---

## 10. Patients (legacy alias)

> Retained for legacy integrations only. New code should hit `/users/*`.

* `GET /api/v1/patients/search?q=…` — same as `GET /users?q=…&type=PATIENT`, returns the minimal `{id, mrn, name, status, floor}` shape.
* `GET /api/v1/patients/active` — currently checked-in patients with their last-known floor + camera.
* `GET /api/v1/patients/{id}` — full profile with relations. Returns any user type, not just patients (the route name predates the unified model).
* `GET /api/v1/patients/{id}/status` — `{id, mrn, name, status, floor, camera_id, last_seen_at}`.

---

## 11. Tracking & presence

Real-time, cross-camera presence is maintained by the camera pipeline and exposed over HTTP for synchronous reads. For an event stream, use the WebSocket (§17).

### `GET /api/v1/tracking/presence`

Cross-camera snapshot, keyed by `user_id` (as string in JSON). Entries older than 10 seconds are dropped on read.

```json
{
  "42": {
    "last_seen": 1748079164.512,
    "cameras": ["cam_lobby_2f", "cam_corridor_3f"]
  }
}
```

> `last_seen` is a **Unix-epoch float** (seconds since 1970), not an ISO timestamp — it comes straight from the event-processor's `time.time()` and is meant for liveness comparisons (`now - last_seen < N`). Convert client-side if you need a date.

### `GET /api/v1/tracking/find?query=…`

Locate one user by free-text. Returns the closest match + the camera name/floor when they are currently inside.

```json
{
  "found": true,
  "patient": { "id": 42, "mrn": "MRN-00042", "name": "Asha Devi" },
  "location": {
    "camera_id": "cam_lobby_2f",
    "camera_name": "Lobby Cam",
    "floor": "floor_2"
  },
  "last_seen_at": "2026-05-24T09:12:44+00:00",
  "status": "IN"
}
```

`found` is `true` only when the user matched **and** is currently inside (`status="IN"`). On a successful name/MRN match for a checked-out user, `found=false` but `patient` is still populated — `location` will be `null` and `status="OUT"`. When no user matched at all, `patient` is `null` too.

### `GET /api/v1/tracking/cameras`

Camera roster joined with current presence. Inactive cameras are omitted. Each entry:

```json
{
  "camera_id": "cam_lobby_2f",
  "name": "Lobby Cam",
  "floor": "floor_2",
  "role": "entry",
  "patients": [
    { "id": 42, "name": "Asha Devi", "status": "IN", "floor": "floor_2", "camera_id": "cam_lobby_2f", "last_seen_at": "…" }
  ]
}
```

### `GET /api/v1/tracking/current`

Flat list of every user with `current_status="IN"`.

### `GET /api/v1/tracking/by-camera`

Same data as `/cameras` but grouped strictly by `camera_id` (without joining the roster name) and including cameras that currently have no one inside.

### `GET /api/v1/tracking/summary`

Totals.

```json
{
  "total_inside": 17,
  "floors": { "floor_1": 4, "floor_2": 9, "floor_3": 4 }
}
```

---

## 12. History

### `GET /api/v1/history/date/{YYYY-MM-DD}`

Every session that started on the given date. Each row:

```json
{
  "patient_id": 42,
  "name": "Asha Devi",
  "user_type": "PATIENT",
  "entry": "2026-05-24T08:55:11+00:00",
  "exit": "2026-05-24T11:14:09+00:00",
  "duration": 8338.0,
  "floor": "floor_2",
  "camera_id": "cam_lobby_2f"
}
```

`exit` and `duration` are `null` for sessions still open.

### `GET /api/v1/history/patient/{patient_id}`

All sessions for one user, newest first. Same row shape minus the user fields.

---

## 13. Cameras admin

Mutations are serialised under an `asyncio.Lock` inside the `CameraRegistry` singleton. If you receive `503`, the camera system has not booted — set `START_CAMERA_SYSTEM=1` in the backend's environment.

### `GET /api/v1/cameras`

List cameras (active + inactive) with runtime `status` ∈ `running | stopped | missing`.

### `GET /api/v1/cameras/{camera_id}`

Single camera.

### `POST /api/v1/cameras`

Create + spawn a worker.

**Body**

```json
{
  "name": "Lobby Cam",
  "type": "rtsp",
  "source": "rtsp://user:pass@10.0.0.31/Streaming/Channels/101",
  "floor": "floor_2",
  "role": "entry",
  "active": true
}
```

* `type` must be `"rtsp"`. Legacy USB records can be imported during the one-time JSON cutover, but new USB cameras are intentionally not creatable from the API.
* `source` must begin with `rtsp://` or `rtsps://`.
* `floor` is lowercased and underscored automatically (`"Floor 2"` → `"floor_2"`).
* `role` is one of `entry | exit | inside`.

**Response 201** — full camera record (server assigns `camera_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`).

**Errors**: `409` on duplicate `name`, `503` if camera system isn't running.

### `PATCH /api/v1/cameras/{camera_id}`

Partial update. The worker is restarted **only** when `source`, `type`, or `active` actually change. Empty body returns the current record (so idempotent retries succeed).

### `DELETE /api/v1/cameras/{camera_id}`

Stop the worker and remove the row. Outstanding session history rows pointing at this camera are left intact.

**Response 204**.

### `POST /api/v1/cameras/{camera_id}/restart`

Bounce the worker without changing config.

### `POST /api/v1/cameras/test`

Probe an RTSP URL without persisting it. Always returns `200` with a structured result so the caller can render either side in one code path:

```json
{ "ok": true,  "width": 1920, "height": 1080, "elapsed_ms": 412, "error": null }
{ "ok": false, "width": null, "height": null, "elapsed_ms": 5001, "error": "timed out" }
```

---

## 14. Front Desk

The Front Desk surface is purpose-built for staffed queue workflows: scan a frame, get the closest-to-camera primary plus everyone else who is identifiable in the same frame as `candidates[]` so the operator can swap who they're serving with one click.

### `POST /api/v1/frontdesk/scan`

Detect + identify every face in an uploaded frame. The closest face (largest bbox area) becomes the primary; the rest are returned as `candidates[]` ranked by `(bbox_area, confidence)` desc.

**Content-Type**: `multipart/form-data`

| Form field | Type | Required |
| ---------- | ---- | -------- |
| `image` | file | yes |

**Response 200**

```json
{
  "matched": true,
  "patient": {
    "id": 42,
    "user_type": "PATIENT",
    "name": "Asha Devi",
    "mrn": "MRN-00042"
  },
  "confidence": 0.91,
  "recent_visits": [
    { "id": 318, "token": "C-12", "status": "DONE", "created_at": "2026-05-22T10:14:00+00:00" }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    {
      "patient_id": 42,
      "name": "Asha Devi",
      "confidence": 0.91,
      "bbox_area": 88420,
      "is_primary": true,
      "patient": { "id": 42, "user_type": "PATIENT", "name": "Asha Devi", "mrn": "MRN-00042" }
    },
    {
      "patient_id": 51,
      "name": "Ravi Devi",
      "confidence": 0.83,
      "bbox_area": 32104,
      "is_primary": false,
      "patient": { "id": 51, "user_type": "RELATIVE", "name": "Ravi Devi" }
    }
  ],
  "unrecognised_count": 1
}
```

* `matched=false` means either no faces were detected, or none cleared the threshold; `patient` and `recent_visits` are absent / `null` but `candidates[]` may still carry secondary recognised faces.
* `unrecognised_count` is the number of detected faces with no FAISS hit — surface as "1 unknown face in frame" in your UI.
* `recent_visits` lists up to the 5 most recent OPD visits for the primary patient (`frontdesk_service.visit_to_dict` shape — `id`, `token`, `status`, `created_at`, etc.). Omitted when `matched=false`.
* Every `candidates[i].patient` carries a full enough record (`_patient_summary`) for the UI to swap without re-scanning.

### `GET /api/v1/frontdesk/search?q=…&limit=10`

Manual fallback for failed face scans. Matches against MRN, phone, and name. Returns the **same shape** as `/scan` (so the UI can swap transparently) — `confidence` is always `null` here, `candidates[]` is the ranked list of partial matches.

### `POST /api/v1/frontdesk/visits`

Create an OPD visit + allocate a token. Broadcasts `frontdesk.visit.created` over `/api/v1/ws/live`.

**Body**

```json
{
  "patient_id": 42,
  "visit_type": "GENERAL",
  "department_id": 1,
  "doctor_id": 7,
  "room_id": 3,
  "note": null,
  "source": "FACE_SCAN",
  "created_by": "operator@hospital"
}
```

* `visit_type`: `GENERAL | SPECIALIST | DOCTOR`.
* `source` defaults to `"FACE_SCAN"`.
* `doctor_id` / `room_id` / `note` / `created_by` optional.

**Response 200** — slip payload (visit row + patient summary + token).

**Errors**: `404` (patient unknown), `400` (invalid visit type / missing required field).

### `GET /api/v1/frontdesk/visits/today?department_id=&status=`

Today's queue. `status` ∈ `WAITING | IN_CONSULT | DONE | CANCELLED`. Returns `{ "visits": [...] }`.

### `GET /api/v1/frontdesk/visits/{visit_id}`

Single visit as a slip payload.

### `PATCH /api/v1/frontdesk/visits/{visit_id}`

Update visit status. Broadcasts `frontdesk.visit.status_changed` over `/api/v1/ws/live`.

```json
{ "status": "IN_CONSULT" }
```

### `POST /api/v1/frontdesk/visits/{visit_id}/reprint`

Mark printed + return the slip payload again. Idempotent.

### `GET /api/v1/frontdesk/visits/by-date/{YYYY-MM-DD}`

Every OPD visit on a given date. `{ "visits": [...] }`.

### `GET /api/v1/frontdesk/visits/{visit_id}/history`

Full status-transition timeline for one visit. `{ "history": [...] }`.

### `GET /api/v1/frontdesk/patients/{patient_id}/visits?limit=50`

History of OPD visits for one patient.

### `GET /api/v1/frontdesk/patients/by-date/{YYYY-MM-DD}`

Distinct patients who had at least one OPD visit on a given date.

## 15. Front Desk admin

Mounted at `/api/v1/frontdesk/admin/*`. CRUD for the lookup tables that Doctor users and patient OPD visits reference. No auth — gate at the proxy.

### Departments

* `GET /frontdesk/admin/departments?include_inactive=false`
* `POST /frontdesk/admin/departments`
* `PATCH /frontdesk/admin/departments/{dept_id}`
* `DELETE /frontdesk/admin/departments/{dept_id}` — soft delete (`is_active=false`).

**Department body**

```json
{ "code": "CARD", "name": "Cardiology", "token_prefix": "C", "default_room_id": 3 }
```

* `code` and `token_prefix` are unique (`409` on conflict).

### Rooms

* `GET /frontdesk/admin/rooms?include_inactive=false`
* `POST /frontdesk/admin/rooms` — `{ "name": "Room 12", "floor": "floor_3", "description": "ECG" }`
* `PATCH /frontdesk/admin/rooms/{room_id}`
* `DELETE /frontdesk/admin/rooms/{room_id}` — soft delete.

### Doctors (lookup-table, not user records)

> The doctor *lookup table* drives department/room assignments. Doctor *user records* live under `/users` with `user_type=DOCTOR` — they reference these IDs via `opd_department_id` / `opd_room_id`.

* `GET /frontdesk/admin/doctors?department_id=&include_inactive=false`
* `POST /frontdesk/admin/doctors` — `{ "name": "Dr. Lee", "department_id": 1, "room_id": 3, "specialty": "Interventional" }`
* `PATCH /frontdesk/admin/doctors/{doctor_id}`
* `DELETE /frontdesk/admin/doctors/{doctor_id}` — soft delete.

## 16. MJPEG streaming

### `GET /api/v1/stream/{camera_id}`

Multipart MJPEG live stream with bbox + identity overlays drawn server-side. Any number of clients can subscribe to the same camera_id concurrently — a single `StreamBroadcaster` per camera does the encode once and fans bytes out to N viewers. Slow viewers locally drop the oldest pending frame.

**Headers**

```
Content-Type: multipart/x-mixed-replace; boundary=frame
```

**Tuning constants** (`stream.py`):

* `TARGET_FPS = 8` — per-viewer cap.
* `JPEG_QUALITY = 70`.
* `IDLE_TIMEOUT = 15s` — broadcaster self-terminates if no frames arrive.

**HTML example**

```html
<img src="http://localhost:8000/api/v1/stream/cam_lobby_2f" />
```

**Errors**: `404` if `camera_id` has no active stream queue (camera not booted, not registered, or was just removed).

### `GET /api/v1/stream/{camera_id}/snapshot`

Single-frame JPEG, **without** overlays — this is what the Front Desk pipeline uses so the recogniser sees the bare frame. Encodes the broadcaster's cached raw BGR frame on demand.

* `200 image/jpeg` on success.
* `404` if camera unknown.
* `503` if no frame arrives within ~1 second (camera idle/paused).

---

## 17. WebSocket live feed

### `WS /api/v1/ws/live`

Server-push event channel. The client should connect, then keep the socket open; messages from the client are silently discarded (used only for liveness detection). All events are JSON.

**Auth** (when `AUTH_ENABLED=true`): the handshake requires a valid session cookie whose account holds `tracking.read`. The cookie rides the WS handshake automatically for a same-origin SPA — no extra client handling. An unauthorized handshake is rejected with close code **4401**; the SPA should treat 4401 as "re-login" and not reconnect-loop.

**Event shape**

```json
{ "type": "DETECTION", "camera_id": "cam_lobby_2f", "faces": [ … ] }
```

Currently emitted types:

| `type` | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `DETECTION` | Per-frame face detections from a camera. `faces[]` carries the same per-face shape as `/recognize` plus a sticky `user_type`. Also populates the server-side detection cache used by the MJPEG overlay path. |
| `frontdesk.visit.created` | Broadcast after `POST /frontdesk/visits` succeeds. Payload: `{ "type": "...", "visit": { … visit_to_dict … } }`. |
| `frontdesk.visit.status_changed` | Broadcast after `PATCH /frontdesk/visits/{id}` succeeds. Same payload shape. |
| (internal) `PRESENCE` | Cross-camera presence snapshot. Consumed by the in-process cache and **not** rebroadcast to clients. |

There is no ack protocol and no replay. If a client misses an event, they must re-query the relevant REST endpoint to resync.

**JavaScript example**

```js
const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8000/api/v1/ws/live");
ws.onmessage = (ev) => {
  const event = JSON.parse(ev.data);
  if (event.type === "DETECTION") {
    handleDetection(event.camera_id, event.faces);
  }
};
```

## 18. Metrics

### `GET /api/v1/metrics?format=json|prom`

Snapshot of the shared cross-process metrics dict maintained by the camera pipeline. Keys look like `camera.cam_lobby_2f.frame_queue_drops_per_sec`.

* `format=json` (default) — raw dict.
* `format=prom` — Prometheus exposition (`text/plain; version=0.0.4`). Dots become underscores; non-numeric values are dropped.

```
camera_cam_lobby_2f_fps 7.8
camera_cam_lobby_2f_frame_queue_drops_per_sec 0
ai_worker_0_inference_ms_p95 38.4
```

This is intentionally minimal. A full `prometheus-client` integration is a future item — today the endpoint is enough for a Grafana scrape.

## 19. Integration recipes

### Onboard a new patient end-to-end

```python
import requests
BASE = "http://localhost:8000/api/v1"

files = [("images", open(p, "rb")) for p in ("front.jpg", "left.jpg", "right.jpg")]
data = {"name": "Asha Devi", "user_type": "PATIENT"}  # MRN auto-issued
user = requests.post(f"{BASE}/register/multi", data=data, files=files).json()
# user == {"success": True, "user_id": 42, "name": "Asha Devi",
#         "mrn": "MRN-A1B2C3", "embeddings_stored": 3}

# Attach a relative
requests.post(f"{BASE}/users", json={"user_type": "RELATIVE", "name": "Ravi Devi"})
# {"id": 51, ...}

requests.post(f"{BASE}/users/42/relations", json={
    "related_user_id": 51, "relation_type": "GUARDIAN"
})
```

### Front-desk scan loop

```python
while True:
    img = grab_frame_from_frontdesk_camera()
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/frontdesk/scan", files={"image": img}).json()

    if not r["candidates"]:
        prompt_register()
        continue

    primary = r["patient"]
    others = [c for c in r["candidates"] if not c["is_primary"]]
    render_queue(primary=primary, swappable=others, unknowns=r["unrecognised_count"])
```

### Subscribe to live detections

```python
import asyncio, json, websockets

async def main():
    async with websockets.connect("ws://localhost:8000/api/v1/ws/live") as ws:
        async for raw in ws:
            ev = json.loads(raw)
            if ev["type"] == "DETECTION":
                print(ev["camera_id"], [f["identity"] for f in ev["faces"]])

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Sync user list (cron-style)

```python
users = requests.get(f"{BASE}/users", params={"type": "DOCTOR", "limit": 1000}).json()
for u in users:
    upsert_to_mirror_system(u)
```

## 20. Notes for production deployments

* **Run behind a reverse proxy** and terminate TLS there. The service ships unencrypted on `0.0.0.0:8000`.
* **Add auth at the proxy** (mTLS, OAuth proxy, or a simple basic-auth layer). There is no internal auth.
* **Set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`** explicitly in non-dev environments — leaving `*` plus a credentialed reverse proxy means any origin can call your API on a user's behalf.
* **Set `DATABASE_URL`** — the default has a placeholder password and points at `localhost`.
* **`SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD`** (default `0.60` in [`backend/config.py`](../backend/config.py)) is the FAISS cosine-similarity cutoff. Raise it for stricter matching (more `"Unknown"`), lower for laxer matching (more false positives). Tune on a labelled set. Note: a separate `SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD=0.45` exists in [`backend/app/core/config.py`](../backend/app/core/config.py) (Pydantic Settings) but is currently unused by the recognition path — the FAISS code reads the module-level constant directly.
* **`START_CAMERA_SYSTEM=1`** must be set in the backend's env to spawn the camera workers. Without it, the `/cameras/*`, `/stream/*`, `/tracking/*`, and `/metrics` endpoints will return empty data or `503`.
* **FAISS persistence** is debounced. On graceful shutdown the lifespan flushes any pending save; on `SIGKILL` you can lose registrations from the debounce window. Prefer `uvicorn`'s default `SIGTERM` path.
* **Rate-limit `/recognize` and `/frontdesk/scan`** at the proxy — each call drives a full detect+embed pipeline and a scan loop without backoff can saturate CPU.
* **MJPEG bandwidth**: at `TARGET_FPS=8`, `JPEG_QUALITY=70`, a 720p stream is ~500 kbps per viewer. Plan accordingly when streaming to remote operators.

For wider architecture context (multi-process layout, camera pipeline, FAISS lifecycle) see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. For per-commit change history see `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. For hardware sizing and camera placement see `docs/HARDWARE_AND_CAMERAS.md`.

## 21. Facility configuration

The deployment contains exactly one facility, created by the initial seed.
There is no facility CRUD or switcher in the application.

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "display_name": "Mednet",
  "code": "MEDNET",
  "address": null,
  "city": null,
  "state": null,
  "pin_code": null,
  "facility_guid": "ce968cc1-9305-4933-a875-STAGE",

  "is_active": true
}
```

## 22. Integrations

Outbound delivery to the B2B partner's HIS. **Staff punches** land in
`punch_export_queue`; **patient pre-registrations** land in the durable
delivery queue. A single background worker drains both with claim-based
concurrency safety, exponential backoff, and dead-lettering after
`EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`. The worker is **dormant until a
`CLIENT_*_API_URL` is configured** (see CONFIGURATION.md §2) — no
request is ever sent to an unset endpoint. These endpoints are for the
admin console to observe and nudge that pipeline.

### `GET /api/v1/integrations/status`

```json
{
  "punch_api_enabled": false,
  "prereg_api_enabled": false,
  "punch_queue":  {"PENDING": 0, "SENDING": 0, "SENT": 0, "FAILED": 0},
  "prereg_queue": {"PENDING": 0, "SENDING": 0, "SENT": 0, "FAILED": 0}
}
```

### `POST /api/v1/integrations/flush`

Wake the worker for an immediate sweep (no-op if dormant). `{"ok": true}`.

### `POST /api/v1/integrations/exports/{export_id}/retry`
### `POST /api/v1/integrations/preregs/{prereg_id}/retry`

Reset a dead-lettered (`FAILED`) row to `PENDING`, clear its attempt
count, and wake the worker. `409` if the row was already `SENT`, `404`
if it doesn't exist. Never sends inline — only reschedules.

## 23. Locations admin

CRUD for locations (`location_master`) — the named, hierarchical places
inside a facility (floor / corridor / room / gate / ward). Cameras and
tracking logs reference these. Managed from Settings → Locations. Soft
delete (`is_active=false`).

Invariants (enforced server-side): a location's parent must be in the
**same facility**, the parent chain must stay acyclic, and
`location_type` is one of `FLOOR|CORRIDOR|ROOM|GATE|WARD|OTHER`.

### `GET /api/v1/locations?include_inactive=false`

```json
{
  "locations": [
    {
      "id": 3, "facility_id": 1, "parent_location_id": 1,
      "name": "Room 12", "location_type": "ROOM",
      "description": null, "is_active": true
    }
  ]
}
```

### `POST /api/v1/locations`

Body: `name` required; optional `location_type`
(default `OTHER`), `parent_location_id`, `description`. `404` for a
missing facility/parent, `400` for an invalid type or a cycle.

### `PATCH /api/v1/locations/{location_id}`

Partial update; `parent_location_id` may be set to `null` to detach.
Same validation as create.

### `DELETE /api/v1/locations/{location_id}`

Soft-delete (`is_active=false`). Returns the updated object.
